cover-letter.title: Cover letter — structure
cover-letter.reply:
Here is the shape I would use for [DEPARTMENT]:

Paragraph 1 — what you work on, in one sentence a committee member outside your area can follow.
Paragraph 2 — the two results that make the case, each given with its consequence rather than its method.
Paragraph 3 — why this department: the group you would overlap with, and the course you would teach.
Paragraph 4 — availability, and what the first three years would look like.

Keep it to one page. The committee reads forty of these in an evening.

tailor-cv.action: Tailor my CV to a posting
tailor-cv.title: Tailoring a CV — three passes
tailor-cv.reply:
Three passes, in this order:

1. Cut what the ad does not ask for. A CV tailored to everything is tailored to nothing.
2. Move the section the ad leads with to the top of page one — a teaching-heavy ad wants teaching above publications.
3. Rewrite the headline in the ad's own words, without overstating the scope of the work.

What survives untouched: publications, references, dates. Those are the parts a committee checks.

parse-posting.title: What to pull out of a posting
parse-posting.reply:
From an ad I would pull out: employer, role, deadline, the documents required, the named contact, and anything phrased as a hard requirement rather than a preference.

The last one is where applications are lost — "must hold the degree by the start date" is a filter, "experience with large-scale systems desirable" is not.

Job scout already does the cheap half of this without a model: save the URL there and it keeps the link and guesses the employer from it.

follow-up.title: Follow-up after no response
follow-up.reply:
Subject: Following up — [ROLE], [DEPARTMENT]

Dear [NAME],

I applied for [ROLE] on [DATE] and wanted to check the committee has everything it needs from me. I am happy to send the outstanding reference letter directly if that is easier.

I remain very interested in the position, and I am glad to answer anything by email.

With thanks,
[YOUR NAME]

interview.title: Interview — six questions to have answered
interview.reply:
Six questions worth having an answer to before the day:

— What is the work about, in ninety seconds, to someone outside your area?
— What would your first grant be, and to which agency?
— Which two courses could you teach next semester at no notice?
— Who here would you collaborate with, and on what?
— What is the weakness in your own result?
— What do you need in year one to do the work?

Write the answers out longhand. The rehearsal is the point, not the notes.

fallback.title: Assistant — example response
fallback.reply:
No model is connected, so this is a canned answer rather than a reply to what you typed.

With one connected, this screen would read your profile, the documents in your Vault and the application you name, then draft against them on your own device. Point jojo at a local OpenAI-compatible server in Settings — vLLM, Ollama or LM Studio.

The five prompts below each have a worked example you can use in the meantime.

device.title: On this device
device.body: Everything you add is written straight to this phone’s own storage as you work — there is nothing to switch on, and nothing leaves the device. Documents you attach are copied into jojo’s own folder, so they survive the original being moved or deleted.
device.copyOut: To get a copy out, use Export below, or Transfer to send everything to your computer over your local network.

model.title: Model
model.intro: A model on a machine you can reach, or one you pay for. Local is the default because it is the only arrangement where your records never leave this device.
model.loopback: That address means “this device”, so on a phone it points at the phone. Use the computer’s address on your network instead — something like 192.168.1.20, or its .local name.
model.endpointOllama: The host and port. No /v1 — jojo uses Ollama’s own endpoint so it can ask it not to truncate.
model.apiKeyHint: Kept on this device only. It is never put in a backup and never sent anywhere but the provider.
model.modelPlaceholder: Found when you test the connection
model.modelHint: What the server reported. Change it if you serve more than one.
model.savedAsHint: What this server is called in the list. Defaults to the model.
model.contextOllama: Tokens. Empty uses {{tokens}} and lets Ollama size itself; a number here is also sent as num_ctx.
model.contextHint: Tokens your deployment can hold. Empty uses {{tokens}}.
model.reasoningDescription: Lets models that can think — gpt-oss, Gemma 4, Qwen3 — reason before answering. Turn it off if replies come back empty on a small model.
model.kept: Kept on this device. The assistant will use this model.
model.remote: This address is not on this device or your local network, so your records will be sent to it — and to whoever runs it.

reader.title: Read my documents
reader.already: This phone already reads Word files, OpenDocument files, decks, saved pages and plain text on its own — nothing to set up and nothing sent anywhere.
reader.pdf: PDFs are the exception. Turning one back into text needs the font tables inside it, which is more than this app carries. For those, run {{name}} on a machine this phone can reach and give its address below.
reader.addressHint: Where markitdown-mcp is listening. The path ends in /mcp.
reader.ok: Documents are sent to that address and nowhere else. Nothing is uploaded.
reader.notice: {{name}} is a separate program, not part of jojo. {{copyright}} {{licence}}. jojo is not affiliated with Microsoft.

Transfer, under More, moves everything to a computer with the documents included.

reset.description: Every edit, addition and deletion from this session is discarded and the seeded records come back exactly as they shipped, so any documents you attached are deleted from this device. Your keyword list itself is left alone. There is no undo.

cloudNotice.headline: Your records leave this device when you use {{name}}

sent.what: Everything the assistant reads to answer you is sent to {{name}}: your applications and notes, your profile, your CV text once a document is read, and the names and email addresses of any referees or recruiters it looks at.
sent.others: Some of that is other people’s personal information, not just yours.
sent.local: With a model on your own machine instead, none of it leaves.

cloudNotice.background: It is not only when you chat. While {{name}} is selected, jojo also sends it records for work done in the background: the duplicate check when you save an application, reading the postings your scout finds, fit readings against your profile, tailoring your CV and letters, and shortening a long conversation so it fits.

cost.paid: {{short}} bills your account, and its own terms govern what it may keep and whether what you send may be used to improve its models.
cost.freeTier: {{short}} has a free tier with limits as well as paid use billed to your account. Either way its own terms govern what it may keep and whether what you send may be used to improve its models.
cost.bargain: That is a different bargain from the local option, not a worse one, but it is worth reading before your records are part of it.

cloudNotice.openrouter: OpenRouter passes each request on to the company that makes the model you pick, under that company’s terms as well as its own. OpenRouter’s own terms let it log requests and use their content in anonymised form.
cloudNotice.business: These API terms are written for businesses and developers. jojo cannot tell you whether they fit a personal job search; checking that they fit your use is up to you.

liability.party: You are the account holder and the party to that agreement — jojo ships no key and makes no request of its own.
liability.breach: Compliance with {{short}}’s terms is yours, and jojo accepts no liability for any breach of them.
